records.statement: CsTPS1FN from Finola was functionally characterized with (−)-limonene as its major product.
records.populationOrMaterial: Heterologously expressed Cannabis sativa Finola CsTPS1FN enzyme
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene synthase enzyme assay with chromatographic product analysis
records.notes: Minor products reported include (+)-α-pinene, camphene, (+)-β-pinene, and myrcene.

records.statement: CsTPS2FN from Finola was functionally characterized with (+)-α-pinene as its major product.
records.populationOrMaterial: Heterologously expressed Cannabis sativa Finola CsTPS2FN enzyme
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene synthase enzyme assay with chromatographic product analysis
records.notes: Minor products reported include (+)-β-pinene, myrcene, (−)-limonene, β-phellandrene, and tentatively identified isoterpinolene.

records.statement: CsTPS3FN from Finola was functionally characterized as a β-myrcene synthase.
records.populationOrMaterial: Heterologously expressed Cannabis sativa Finola CsTPS3FN enzyme
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene synthase enzyme assay with chromatographic product analysis

records.statement: CsTPS5FN from Finola produced β-myrcene among its major products.
records.populationOrMaterial: Heterologously expressed Cannabis sativa Finola CsTPS5FN enzyme
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene synthase enzyme assay with chromatographic product analysis
records.notes: The same enzyme also produced (−)-α-pinene as a major product.

records.statement: CsTPS6FN from Finola was functionally characterized with (E)-β-ocimene as its major product.
records.populationOrMaterial: Heterologously expressed Cannabis sativa Finola CsTPS6FN enzyme
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene synthase enzyme assay with chromatographic product analysis

records.statement: CsTPS9FN from Finola was functionally characterized with β-caryophyllene among its major sesquiterpene products.
records.populationOrMaterial: Heterologously expressed Cannabis sativa Finola CsTPS9FN enzyme
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene synthase enzyme assay with chromatographic product analysis
records.notes: α-Humulene was also a major product.

records.statement: CsTPS9FN from Finola was functionally characterized with α-humulene among its major sesquiterpene products.
records.populationOrMaterial: Heterologously expressed Cannabis sativa Finola CsTPS9FN enzyme
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene synthase enzyme assay with chromatographic product analysis
records.notes: β-Caryophyllene was also a major product.

records.statement: CsTPS13PK from Purple Kush was functionally characterized with (Z)-β-ocimene as its major product.
records.populationOrMaterial: Heterologously expressed Cannabis sativa Purple Kush CsTPS13PK enzyme
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene synthase enzyme assay with chromatographic product analysis

records.statement: CsTPS33PK from Purple Kush was functionally characterized with α-terpinene and γ-terpinene as major products.
records.populationOrMaterial: Heterologously expressed Cannabis sativa Purple Kush CsTPS33PK enzyme
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene synthase enzyme assay with chromatographic product analysis
records.notes: This evidence record is keyed to α-terpinene; γ-terpinene is retained in the gene product list.

records.statement: CsTPS5FN from Finola produced (−)-α-pinene among its major products.
records.populationOrMaterial: Heterologously expressed Cannabis sativa Finola CsTPS5FN enzyme
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene synthase enzyme assay with chromatographic product analysis
records.notes: β-Myrcene was also a major product.

records.statement: CsTPS33PK from Purple Kush was functionally characterized with α-terpinene and γ-terpinene as major products.
records.populationOrMaterial: Heterologously expressed Cannabis sativa Purple Kush CsTPS33PK enzyme
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene synthase enzyme assay with chromatographic product analysis
records.notes: This evidence record is keyed to γ-terpinene; α-terpinene is retained in the gene product list.

records.statement: In the reported cannabis inflorescence storage experiments, most control samples lost terpene content over storage, and loss rates differed between harvests and sample conditions.
records.populationOrMaterial: Cannabis inflorescence from DJ's Gold and Cream Caramel chemotypes stored under study-specific packaging conditions
records.analyticalMethod: Headspace gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS GC-MS)
records.notes: System-level post-harvest evidence. Do not assign the reported total-terpene loss rate to every individual terpene, cultivar, storage container, or environment.

records.statement: The d-limonene safety review reported dermal irritation or sensitization concerns associated particularly with oxidation products or metabolites under relevant consumer-product exposure contexts.
records.populationOrMaterial: Toxicology and human/animal safety literature reviewed for d-limonene
records.notes: This record does not establish cannabis inhalation safety or a universal exposure threshold.

records.statement: Air exposure caused linalool autoxidation with formation of hydroperoxides and secondary oxidation products identified using chromatographic and spectroscopic methods.
records.populationOrMaterial: Pure and air-exposed linalool plus isolated oxidation products
records.analyticalMethod: Flash chromatography, preparative HPLC, NMR, GC/MS, GC and HPLC quantification
records.notes: Supports oxidation chemistry under the study conditions; not a universal storage-rate estimate for cannabis flower.

records.statement: In the reported local lymph node assay, pure linalool showed no sensitizing potential while air-exposed linalool samples produced positive responses, with hydroperoxides among the strongest tested allergens.
records.populationOrMaterial: Local lymph node assay comparing pure linalool, air-exposed linalool, and isolated oxidation products
records.analyticalMethod: Local lymph node assay
records.notes: Animal sensitization evidence tied to oxidized linalool; not direct evidence for every human exposure route.

records.statement: The RIFM fragrance-use safety assessment reported no genotoxicity signal and no skin-sensitization concern at the declared use levels evaluated, while other endpoints were assessed using exposure-based approaches.
records.populationOrMaterial: Integrated fragrance-ingredient safety assessment for β-caryophyllene
records.notes: Applies to the exposure assumptions and declared fragrance-use levels in the assessment; it is not a blanket cannabis inhalation-safety claim.

records.statement: The β-myrcene review found that much of the proposed biological research was based on non-human studies and that human studies were lacking.
records.populationOrMaterial: Published β-myrcene phytochemistry, biological, and toxicology literature
records.notes: This is an evidence-gap statement and should not be interpreted as proof of either safety or harm.

records.statement: A 10-year human patch-testing study evaluated contact allergy to hydroperoxides formed by autoxidation of limonene, supporting the clinical relevance of oxidized limonene in contact-allergy assessment.
records.populationOrMaterial: Dermatology patients patch tested for hydroperoxides of limonene over a 10-year period
records.analyticalMethod: Clinical patch testing
records.notes: Contact-allergy context only; does not establish inhalation risk or typical cannabis exposure.

records.statement: A 10-year human patch-testing study evaluated contact allergy to hydroperoxides formed by autoxidation of linalool, supporting the clinical relevance of oxidized linalool in contact-allergy assessment.
records.populationOrMaterial: Dermatology patients patch tested for hydroperoxides of linalool over a 10-year period
records.analyticalMethod: Clinical patch testing
records.notes: Contact-allergy context only; does not establish inhalation risk or typical cannabis exposure.

records.statement: The 2026 NTP report evaluated subchronic and chronic whole-body inhalation exposure to α-pinene in rats and mice and reported exposure-related target-organ and neoplastic findings in specific animal groups at the tested concentrations.
records.populationOrMaterial: Sprague Dawley rats, B6C3F1/N mice, and CD-1 mice exposed by whole-body inhalation
records.analyticalMethod: Controlled whole-body inhalation; pathology, reproductive endpoints, and internal α-pinene/α-pinene oxide measurements including GC-MS methods
records.notes: Animal hazard evidence at controlled inhalation concentrations. Do not convert these findings into a human cannabis-use threshold or claim of equivalent exposure.

records.statement: A systematic review of terpinolene research concluded that in-vivo efficacy and safety had been poorly evaluated through preclinical and clinical trials and called for substantially better characterization.
records.populationOrMaterial: Systematic review of 57 included terpinolene studies selected from four bibliographic databases
records.analyticalMethod: PRISMA-guided systematic review
records.notes: Evidence-gap record. It does not prove terpinolene is safe or unsafe; it documents insufficient depth of in-vivo and clinical safety evidence.

records.statement: In the reported acute dermal irritation assay, β-pinene produced a positive response at the tested 4% concentration.
records.populationOrMaterial: Experimental dermal irritation testing of major myoga volatile constituents
records.analyticalMethod: Acute dermal irritation assay; Guinea-pig Maximization test used in the broader study
records.notes: Dermal, concentration-specific animal evidence only; this record does not establish inhalation risk or typical cannabis exposure.

records.statement: In adult zebrafish given α-humulene by intraperitoneal injection, the study reported low acute toxicity within the tested model, with LD50 greater than 40 mg/kg.
records.populationOrMaterial: Adult zebrafish (Danio rerio) given α-humulene by intraperitoneal injection
records.analyticalMethod: Acute toxicity and behavioral assays
records.notes: Acute zebrafish injection model only. This is not direct human evidence and not a cannabis inhalation safety threshold.

records.statement: In the Babbas Erkle Cookies accession, β-myrcene concentration differed across the tested light spectra, with purple and blue treatments among the highest measured conditions.
records.populationOrMaterial: Cannabis sativa 'Babbas Erkle Cookies' grown under HPS and five LED spectral treatments
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene quantification of harvested inflorescences under controlled light treatments
records.notes: Treatment-specific result in one accession. Do not generalize the ranking of spectra to all genotypes or facilities.

records.statement: In the same controlled light experiment, limonene concentration varied by spectral treatment, with the purple treatment higher than amber and red among the reported comparisons.
records.populationOrMaterial: Cannabis sativa 'Babbas Erkle Cookies' grown under HPS and five LED spectral treatments
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene quantification of harvested inflorescences under controlled light treatments
records.notes: Single-accession, treatment-specific result.

records.statement: β-Pinene concentration varied across the tested light treatments in Babbas Erkle Cookies, with purple and blue treatments among the higher reported conditions.
records.populationOrMaterial: Cannabis sativa 'Babbas Erkle Cookies' grown under HPS and five LED spectral treatments
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene quantification of harvested inflorescences under controlled light treatments
records.notes: Does not establish a universal blue/purple-light rule.

records.statement: Linalool concentration differed among the tested light spectra, with purple and blue treatments among the higher reported conditions in the studied accession.
records.populationOrMaterial: Cannabis sativa 'Babbas Erkle Cookies' grown under HPS and five LED spectral treatments
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene quantification of harvested inflorescences under controlled light treatments
records.notes: Treatment-specific and genotype-specific result.

records.statement: The greenhouse study found significant interactions among light spectrum, strain, and flower position for α-pinene, including strong strain-dependent differences in concentration.
records.populationOrMaterial: Three Cannabis sativa strains grown under three light spectra with multiple flower positions sampled
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene analysis of flowers from defined plant positions under controlled greenhouse lighting
records.notes: Supports genotype × environment × flower-position interaction, not a universal spectrum ranking.

records.statement: Humulene showed significant interactions between light spectrum and strain in the reported greenhouse experiment, indicating that lighting effects depended on genetic background.
records.populationOrMaterial: Three Cannabis sativa strains grown under three light spectra
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene analysis of flowers under controlled greenhouse lighting
records.notes: Do not generalize across cultivars.

records.statement: β-Caryophyllene showed significant light-spectrum × strain interactions in the greenhouse study, reinforcing that environmental responses were genotype-dependent.
records.populationOrMaterial: Three Cannabis sativa strains grown under three light spectra
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene analysis of flowers under controlled greenhouse lighting
records.notes: Genotype-dependent cultivation-factor evidence.

records.statement: Linalool showed significant interactions between light spectrum and strain in the greenhouse experiment, demonstrating that spectrum effects were not uniform across genetic backgrounds.
records.populationOrMaterial: Three Cannabis sativa strains grown under three light spectra
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene analysis of flowers under controlled greenhouse lighting
records.notes: Supports interaction, not a universal spectrum prescription.

records.statement: β-Myrcene changed across drying conditions in the studied medicinal cannabis chemovars, and controlled-atmosphere approaches preserved volatile terpene content differently from traditional drying.
records.populationOrMaterial: Medicinal cannabis chemovars 240 and Gen12 subjected to controlled-atmosphere and traditional drying
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene quantification before and after defined drying treatments
records.notes: Cultivar- and drying-condition-specific. Do not generalize exact preservation rates.

records.statement: α-Pinene concentrations differed among controlled-atmosphere and traditional drying conditions in the tested medicinal cannabis material.
records.populationOrMaterial: Medicinal cannabis chemovars 240 and Gen12 under four drying conditions
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene quantification before and after defined drying treatments
records.notes: Treatment-specific post-harvest evidence.

records.statement: β-Pinene concentrations were measured before and after controlled-atmosphere and traditional drying, with preservation patterns depending on the drying treatment and chemovar.
records.populationOrMaterial: Medicinal cannabis chemovars 240 and Gen12 under four drying conditions
records.analyticalMethod: Terpene quantification before and after defined drying treatments
records.notes: Chemovar- and treatment-specific.

records.statement: In the reported medical cannabis experiment, light spectrum and PPFD interacted with terpenoid accumulation, and one dual-red-peak white-light treatment increased total terpenoid concentration at high PPFD relative to the other tested spectra.
records.populationOrMaterial: Medical Cannabis sativa grown under controlled spectra at two PPFD levels
records.analyticalMethod: Specialized-metabolite quantification under controlled light treatments
records.notes: System-level cultivation evidence; not a universal lighting recommendation and not compound-specific.

records.statement: In the reported two-cultivar dried-hemp experiment, myrcene was among the monoterpenes that showed measurable post-harvest loss, including a noticeable reduction after electron-beam treatment and continued storage-related decline.
records.populationOrMaterial: Dried flowers from two hemp cultivars stored for 12 weeks, with irradiated and non-irradiated groups
records.analyticalMethod: Quantitative terpene analysis across treatment and storage time points
records.notes: Cultivar- and treatment-specific post-harvest evidence. Do not convert this to a universal myrcene loss percentage.

records.statement: Limonene decreased following electron-beam treatment in the reported dried-hemp study, and storage time contributed substantially to terpene variability over the 12-week experiment.
records.populationOrMaterial: Dried flowers from two hemp cultivars stored for 12 weeks, with irradiated and non-irradiated groups
records.analyticalMethod: Quantitative terpene analysis across treatment and storage time points
records.notes: Treatment- and cultivar-specific evidence; not a universal limonene shelf-life value.

records.statement: Terpinolene showed decreased levels following electron-beam treatment in the cultivar where it was quantifiable, within a broader pattern of storage-driven terpene loss.
records.populationOrMaterial: Dried flowers from two hemp cultivars stored for 12 weeks, with irradiated and non-irradiated groups
records.analyticalMethod: Quantitative terpene analysis across treatment and storage time points
records.notes: Terpinolene was below quantification in one cultivar; this record preserves that study-specific limitation.

records.statement: Alpha-pinene was less affected by electron-beam treatment than the more labile major monoterpenes in the reported hemp study, though slight reductions were observed and storage time remained an important driver of terpene change.
records.populationOrMaterial: Dried flowers from two hemp cultivars stored for 12 weeks, with irradiated and non-irradiated groups
records.analyticalMethod: Quantitative terpene analysis across treatment and storage time points
records.notes: Relative treatment sensitivity is study-specific and does not establish universal alpha-pinene stability.

records.statement: Beta-pinene was less affected by electron-beam treatment than the more labile major monoterpenes in the reported hemp study, though slight reductions were observed and storage time remained an important driver of terpene change.
records.populationOrMaterial: Dried flowers from two hemp cultivars stored for 12 weeks, with irradiated and non-irradiated groups
records.analyticalMethod: Quantitative terpene analysis across treatment and storage time points
records.notes: Relative treatment sensitivity is study-specific and does not establish universal beta-pinene stability.

records.statement: Trans-caryophyllene was comparatively less affected immediately by electron-beam treatment than the major monoterpenes in the reported hemp study, consistent with the broader class-level finding that sesquiterpenes were less affected than monoterpenes.
records.populationOrMaterial: Dried flowers from two hemp cultivars stored for 12 weeks, with irradiated and non-irradiated groups
records.analyticalMethod: Quantitative terpene analysis across treatment and storage time points
records.notes: Comparative treatment sensitivity only; not a universal caryophyllene preservation claim.

records.statement: Linalool was comparatively less affected immediately by electron-beam treatment in the reported two-cultivar hemp study, though slight reductions were observed and storage still altered the overall terpene profile.
records.populationOrMaterial: Dried flowers from two hemp cultivars stored for 12 weeks, with irradiated and non-irradiated groups
records.analyticalMethod: Quantitative terpene analysis across treatment and storage time points
records.notes: Study-specific treatment/storage evidence; not a universal linalool stability rule.

records.statement: Alpha-humulene showed minimal immediate difference between irradiated and non-irradiated groups in the reported hemp study, while longer-term storage remained the dominant factor affecting the terpene profile overall.
records.populationOrMaterial: Dried flowers from two hemp cultivars stored for 12 weeks, with irradiated and non-irradiated groups
records.analyticalMethod: Quantitative terpene analysis across treatment and storage time points
records.notes: Immediate treatment comparison and overall storage context only; do not infer a universal humulene loss rate.

records.statement: (E)-β-caryophyllene selectively bound to the CB2 receptor and functioned as a CB2 agonist in the reported mechanistic assays.
records.populationOrMaterial: Receptor-binding systems and primary human monocytes used for downstream signaling assays
records.analyticalMethod: Receptor binding, molecular docking, second-messenger and kinase-signaling assays
records.notes: Mechanistic receptor evidence only. It does not establish a therapeutic outcome in humans or prove that cannabis exposure reaches the same effective concentration.

records.statement: In a short controlled human inhalation experiment, the β-caryophyllene group showed a decrease in anxiety scores after stress tasks and distinct physiological/EEG responses compared with the odorless control condition.
records.populationOrMaterial: 12 healthy participants assigned to the β-caryophyllene inhalation group within a 48-person four-group experiment
records.analyticalMethod: Controlled odor inhalation with STAI, EEG, facial-expression, heart-rate, blood-pressure and subjective measures
records.notes: Small, short-duration controlled experiment in healthy participants. Supports only the measured acute responses under this protocol and is not clinical efficacy evidence.

records.statement: In the same controlled human experiment, linalool inhalation produced physiological changes including a statistically significant systolic-blood-pressure difference, but the abstract did not report the anxiety-score decrease observed for β-caryophyllene and citral.
records.populationOrMaterial: 12 healthy participants assigned to the linalool inhalation group within a 48-person four-group experiment
records.analyticalMethod: Controlled odor inhalation with STAI, EEG, facial-expression, heart-rate, blood-pressure and subjective measures
records.notes: Preserves a mixed/null outcome rather than implying linalool reproduced the β-caryophyllene anxiety result. Short-duration human experiment, not therapeutic efficacy evidence.

records.statement: Myrcene produced antinociceptive/peripheral analgesic responses in the reported rat and mouse experimental models.
records.populationOrMaterial: Rat hyperalgesia models and mouse contortion model using isolated/commercial myrcene
records.analyticalMethod: Behavioral nociception and hyperalgesia assays
records.notes: Animal pharmacology only. Does not establish pain relief in humans, a cannabis product, or any specific inhaled dose.

records.statement: In 20 healthy volunteers, inhaled (+)- and (−)-limonene produced different autonomic and subjective-response patterns, supporting the importance of stereochemical form and odor appraisal in human fragrance experiments.
records.populationOrMaterial: 20 healthy volunteers tested in separate fragrance-inhalation sessions
records.analyticalMethod: Inhalation exposure with autonomic nervous system measures and visual-analog self-evaluation
records.notes: Small healthy-volunteer study of fragrance inhalation. Responses were partly related to subjective odor evaluation and should not be generalized to cannabis effects.

records.statement: In a controlled human exposure-chamber study, d-limonene showed high pulmonary uptake and measurable systemic elimination kinetics; the highest tested exposure was associated with a decrease in vital capacity without reported irritative or CNS symptoms.
records.populationOrMaterial: Human volunteers exposed for two hours at approximately 10, 225, and 450 mg/m³ d-limonene while performing light work
records.analyticalMethod: Controlled inhalation exposure with blood/urine/expired-air toxicokinetics and pulmonary-function testing
records.notes: Occupational-style controlled exposure conditions. Does not represent typical cannabis inhalation concentration, duration, or formulation.

records.statement: In adult zebrafish, intraperitoneal α-humulene produced an anxiolytic-like behavioral response in the light/dark test, with the largest reported effect at an intermediate tested dose.
records.populationOrMaterial: Adult zebrafish given α-humulene by intraperitoneal injection
records.analyticalMethod: Light/dark and locomotor behavioral assays with pharmacological antagonist experiments
records.unit: mg/kg tested dose with maximal reported anxiolytic-like effect
records.notes: Animal behavioral model and injection route only. Not direct evidence of anxiolytic efficacy in humans or of effects from inhaled cannabis.

records.statement: A 2022 review of selected monoterpenes included α-terpinene among compounds with reported toxicological concerns in the literature and emphasized that adverse effects depend on compound, dose, model, and exposure context.
records.populationOrMaterial: Review of in vitro and in vivo toxicological literature for selected monoterpenes and monoterpene-rich essential oils
records.analyticalMethod: Narrative literature review based on selected Scopus-indexed studies
records.notes: This review-level record does not establish a cannabis inhalation threshold or a universal toxicity value for α-terpinene.

records.statement: A mixed toxicogenetic study reported model-dependent γ-terpinene effects including moderate Artemia salina toxicity, reduced Allium cepa mitotic activity, and binucleated-cell changes at the highest tested rat dose, while calling for further work to define limiting doses.
records.populationOrMaterial: Artemia salina, Allium cepa meristematic cells, cultured mammalian cells, erythrocytes, and spontaneously hypertensive rats
records.analyticalMethod: In silico docking plus in vitro, plant-cell, invertebrate, and in vivo toxicogenetic/antioxidant assays
records.notes: Model-specific toxicogenetic evidence. Do not convert the reported endpoints into a human cannabis-use safety threshold.

records.statement: In a 90-day human oral supplementation study using 13.5 or 27 g/day squalene, investigators reported frequent loose stool and concluded that the risk-benefit ratio of the high-dose regimen was too unfavorable to recommend for skin-ageing treatment.
records.populationOrMaterial: 40 women older than 50 years receiving 13.5 g/day or 27 g/day oral squalene for 90 days
records.analyticalMethod: Human supplementation intervention with clinical and skin biomarker assessments
records.notes: High-dose oral supplementation evidence only; not a cannabis inhalation or typical dietary-exposure study.

records.statement: EFSA concluded that background dietary β-carotene was not indicated to cause adverse effects, but available evidence did not support establishing a tolerable upper level for supplemental β-carotene; smokers were advised to avoid β-carotene-containing supplements because lung-cancer risk was the critical concern.
records.populationOrMaterial: Human dietary and supplement evidence reviewed for European risk assessment, including higher-risk smoking populations
records.analyticalMethod: EFSA scientific opinion based on systematic literature review and nutrient risk assessment
records.notes: Applies to dietary/supplemental β-carotene risk assessment. It is not an inhaled-cannabis exposure assessment.

records.statement: A RIFM safety assessment for 3,7-dimethyl-1,3,6-octatriene (CAS 13877-91-3) evaluated genotoxicity, repeated-dose, developmental/reproductive, local respiratory, phototoxicity/photoallergenicity, skin-sensitization, and environmental endpoints under fragrance-use exposure assumptions.
records.populationOrMaterial: Integrated fragrance-ingredient safety assessment using target data, read-across, threshold-of-toxicological-concern, and exposure-based approaches
records.notes: Identity scope is unresolved β-ocimene / 3,7-dimethyl-1,3,6-octatriene. This record must not be counted as E- or Z-β-ocimene isomer-specific evidence.

records.statement: In LPS-stimulated mouse peritoneal macrophages, α-pinene reduced IL-6, TNF-α, nitric oxide, iNOS and COX-2 responses and attenuated MAPK and NF-κB activation under the study conditions.
records.populationOrMaterial: Mouse peritoneal macrophages stimulated with lipopolysaccharide
records.analyticalMethod: Inflammatory mediator measurements and signaling-pathway assays
records.notes: Cell-based anti-inflammatory/mechanistic evidence only; not a human clinical anti-inflammatory claim.

records.statement: In an in-vitro vapor assay, β-pinene vapor inhibited the tested Gram-positive bacterial isolates, while the Gram-negative isolates showed greater resistance under the reported conditions.
records.populationOrMaterial: Fourteen bacterial isolates exposed to β-pinene and citrus-essential-oil vapors
records.analyticalMethod: Bioautography, APCI-MS/SPME-GC-MS vapor characterization, and microbial inhibition assays
records.notes: Laboratory antimicrobial-vapor evidence only. It does not establish clinical antimicrobial efficacy or a cannabis inhalation effect.

records.statement: A systematic review of 57 included terpinolene studies identified multiple reported biological activities, with antioxidant, larvicidal and insecticidal effects among the most prominent, while emphasizing limited mechanistic, preclinical and clinical depth.
records.populationOrMaterial: Systematic review of terpinolene in-silico, in-vitro and in-vivo studies published through June 2020
records.analyticalMethod: PRISMA-guided systematic review across Embase, Web of Science, Scopus and PubMed
records.notes: Review-level biological-activity evidence. The review explicitly notes that most included studies were superficial and that preclinical/clinical characterization remained limited.

records.statement: In isolated rat tracheal smooth muscle, α-terpinene relaxed contractions induced by potassium, acetylcholine and serotonin, with results consistent with inhibition of L-type voltage-gated calcium-channel-dependent contraction.
records.populationOrMaterial: Isolated rat tracheal smooth muscle studied in organ baths
records.analyticalMethod: Isometric contraction recording in isolated tracheal preparations
records.notes: Ex-vivo isolated-organ evidence only; it does not establish respiratory therapeutic efficacy in humans.

records.statement: Gamma-terpinene produced dose-dependent in-vitro activity against Leishmania major promastigotes and amastigotes and altered parasite/macrophage molecular endpoints in the reported experimental system.
records.populationOrMaterial: Leishmania major promastigotes/amastigotes and a murine macrophage model
records.analyticalMethod: MTT assays, cytokine/metacaspase RT-PCR, ROS/antioxidant assays, hemolysis measurements and DNA-fragmentation analysis
records.notes: In-vitro/in-silico antiparasitic evidence. The authors state that further in-vivo and clinical studies are needed.

records.statement: A systematic review summarized in-vitro and in-vivo research reporting antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, lipid-metabolism and other biological actions of squalene, while also reviewing its bioavailability and intracellular transport.
records.populationOrMaterial: Systematic review of recent squalene studies spanning cell, animal and human/bioavailability research
records.analyticalMethod: Systematic literature review
records.notes: Review-level summary across heterogeneous models; it does not establish a universal therapeutic effect or an inhaled-cannabis outcome.

records.statement: In 22 adults given 6 mg deuterium-labeled β-carotene, stable-isotope measurements demonstrated conversion of β-carotene to retinol over 56 days, with substantial inter-individual variability in the conversion factor.
records.populationOrMaterial: 22 adult volunteers given labeled β-carotene and labeled retinyl acetate reference doses
records.analyticalMethod: Stable-isotope feeding design with serial blood sampling, HPLC separation and GC-MS measurement
records.unit: mean beta-carotene:retinol conversion factor by weight
records.notes: Human metabolic conversion evidence at the tested oral dose. It is not evidence for a general supplement benefit or cannabis exposure effect.

records.statement: In the 33-chemovar Cannabis metabolomics study, trans-β-ocimene was detected in the analyzed flower profiles and was among terpenes reported as predominant in higher-CBD chemovars.
records.populationOrMaterial: Thirty-three Cannabis sativa chemovars obtained from five licensed Canadian producers
records.analyticalMethod: Headspace GC-MS terpene metabolomics with reference standards and retention-index confirmation
records.notes: The paper uses trans-β-ocimene terminology; this chapter maps trans to the reviewed (E)-β-ocimene identity.

records.statement: A validated headspace GC-MS-TOF study confirmed cis-β-ocimene in both analyzed Cannabis chemotypes and reported it among the major terpenoids contributing to more than 80% of total terpenoid abundance.
records.populationOrMaterial: Cannabis sativa samples representing two analyzed plant chemotypes
records.analyticalMethod: Headspace gas chromatography coupled to time-of-flight mass spectrometry using terpenoid reference standards
records.notes: The source reports cis-β-ocimene; this chapter maps cis to the reviewed (Z)-β-ocimene identity.

records.statement: α-Terpinene was detected in the 33-chemovar Cannabis terpene-metabolomics study and was strongly correlated with the terpinolene-rich monoterpene profile observed in a subset of chemovars.
records.populationOrMaterial: Thirty-three Cannabis sativa chemovars obtained from five licensed Canadian producers
records.analyticalMethod: Headspace GC-MS terpene metabolomics with external standards and retention-index confirmation
records.notes: Occurrence is study-specific and does not imply universal abundance in Cannabis.

records.statement: γ-Terpinene was detected in the 33-chemovar Cannabis terpene-metabolomics study as part of the strongly correlated terpinolene-associated monoterpene profile.
records.populationOrMaterial: Thirty-three Cannabis sativa chemovars obtained from five licensed Canadian producers
records.analyticalMethod: Headspace GC-MS terpene metabolomics with external standards and retention-index confirmation
records.notes: Occurrence is study-specific and does not imply universal abundance in Cannabis.

records.statement: The Cannabis metabolomics paper lists trans-β-ocimene with citrus/tropical scent descriptors in its terpene sensory table.
records.populationOrMaterial: Literature-linked scent descriptors compiled in the Cannabis terpene metabolomics study
records.notes: Descriptor evidence is sensory language, not proof that trans/(E)-β-ocimene alone determines a sample's aroma.

records.statement: The Cannabis metabolomics paper lists cis-β-ocimene with citrus/tropical scent descriptors in its terpene sensory table.
records.populationOrMaterial: Literature-linked scent descriptors compiled in the Cannabis terpene metabolomics study
records.notes: Descriptor evidence is sensory language, not proof that cis/(Z)-β-ocimene alone determines a sample's aroma.

records.statement: The Cannabis metabolomics paper lists α-terpinene with a woody scent descriptor in its terpene sensory table.
records.populationOrMaterial: Literature-linked scent descriptors compiled in the Cannabis terpene metabolomics study
records.notes: A source-linked descriptor is not a one-compound diagnosis of whole-flower aroma.

records.statement: The Cannabis metabolomics paper lists γ-terpinene with a citrus scent descriptor in its terpene sensory table.
records.populationOrMaterial: Literature-linked scent descriptors compiled in the Cannabis terpene metabolomics study
records.notes: A source-linked descriptor is not a one-compound diagnosis of whole-flower aroma.
